conditions.condition: Globals: SET / KILL subtree / `$GET` / `$DATA`; a rollback restores a killed subtree
Nesting: `TSTART` nests; inner `TCOMMIT` only lowers `$TLEVEL`; a later outer rollback undoes inner work
Partial rollback: `TROLLBACK 1` undoes only the top level, globals and SQL rows alike
`$INCREMENT`: not undone by rollback
Process-private globals: not undone by rollback; invisible to other processes
Visibility: no isolation for globals; SQL SELECT reads uncommitted rows (READ UNCOMMITTED)
Rollback over another's write: a rollback does not overwrite a node another process changed after this process wrote it
SQL `START TRANSACTION`: does nothing when any level is open; else opens level 1
SQL `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK` statements: end one level
Driver `commit()` / `rollback()`: `commit()` ends one level; `rollback()` ends every level

Autocommit: default on; with it off the first DML opens a level SQL owns; turning it on while a level is open commits one level, as `commit()` does, whether it was off or already on and whoever opened the level (revised after round r4; env/explore-9); turning it off inside a transaction is outside the subset
Locks: deferral: an unlock inside a transaction, including release-all and a lock taken before it, takes effect when the outermost transaction ends; an immediate unlock releases at once
Locks: lifetime: a lock not unlocked survives the commit
Locks: names: hierarchical: a name conflicts with ancestors and descendants; siblings do not
Locks: modes: shared locks are compatible; exclusive conflicts with shared, incl. across the hierarchy
Locks: counts: incremental
Non-incremental `LOCK`: releases every held lock first, then locks
Lock wait: a waiting lock is granted when the holder releases; timeout 0 answers `$TEST`
conditions.relied_on_by: head lock waits (30 s), AdjW (5 s)

conditions.condition: Row locks: a DELETE/UPDATE waits for a row another open transaction inserted or updated; after that transaction rolls back it affects nothing; an autocommit statement holds no row lock afterwards; a global SET takes no lock
Unique keys: INSERT of a key another transaction inserted fails at once (-119)
Process stop: rolls back every level and releases every lock; a waiter proceeds
Caller identity: SQL on a cursor and the Native API on the same connection run in one server process (same `$JOB`)
